extra: First $0500 bytes of the mission payload.
Second destination for the mission payload, $3EF0 bytes.

comments.text: Twenty consecutive 64-byte sprite slots in VIC bank $4000. Each slot begins with 21 rows of three pixel bytes, and the last byte is outside the displayed height.
Four sprite slots after the first sixteen mission frames. The VIC slot positions relative to bank $4000 are $A0-$A3.

Four rows of four character codes per 16-byte tile. The map renderer resolves a tile ID through the resident screen-code pointer tables, then indexes this pattern with the character coordinates modulo four.
The stage maps can reference tile ID $44 here. Four character rows at $C440 form its 16-byte shape.
Dictionary slots for tile IDs $45–$84. All sixteen character indices in each slot are zero. The renderer resolves these slots through the same resident pointer tables as the populated patterns.
Dictionary slots for tile IDs $85–$AF. All sixteen character indices in each slot are zero. The renderer resolves these slots through the same resident pointer tables as the populated patterns.
Complete 256-glyph source for the $ADF7 scene. Each glyph occupies eight bytes. The masked wipe at $1E17 reads from this base with an eight-byte stride and writes the corresponding row at $4000.
Tile-indexed colour bytes. The initial playfield renderer at $17CD reads these in parallel with the tile character pointers and $1882 writes the chosen value to colour RAM.
Primary 256-character graphics source. The resident wipe routine at $1DC2 enables RAM under I/O and copies the selected pixel rows to the live character set at $4000.
Rows for character codes $80-$FF in the main stage's 256-glyph set. The masked copy selects them through the same eight-byte stride as the lower codes.
Alternate 256-character graphics source in RAM below the I/O window. The resident wipe routine chooses this source when $1902 is set, unless the alternate scene flag $ADF7 takes priority.
The upper half of the alternate stage's eight-byte character slots, read under CIA and expansion register addresses with I/O banked out.
Stage 1 grid, 64 entries per row and first 9 rows. Each byte selects one 4 × 4 character tile through the split table at $08D6/$09C6.
Stage 1 grid, 64 entries per row and first 9 rows. The engine uses the low three bits for world-coordinate attribute lookups.
Stage 2 grid, 32 entries per row and first 31 rows. Each byte selects one 4 × 4 character tile through the split table at $08D6/$09C6.
Stage 2 tile grid from row 32, column 1. The grid has 32 cells per row. Each byte supplies a metatile index to the renderer through the stage row pointers.
The declared stage-two tile grid is followed by two more rows at stride 32. The first alternates tiles two and three. The second alternates zero and one, repeating the last declared row.

96 loaded bytes after the two retained striped rows and before the attribute grid at $E920. 5 aligned groups of four bytes are $00,$FF,$FF,$00. The stage-two tile row builder stops at $E860, and a controlled draw from character row 107 made no reads here. The original purpose remains open.
Stage 2 grid, 32 entries per row and first 31 rows. The engine uses the low three bits for world-coordinate attribute lookups.
Stage 2 attribute grid from row 32, column 1. The grid has 32 cells per row. Each byte holds the attributes for the matching metatile. The coordinate lookup at $3DFA takes its low three bits.
Five zero-filled rows at the stage-two attribute grid stride of 32 follow the declared grid.
Stage 3 grid, 68 entries per row and first 9 rows. Each byte selects one 4 × 4 character tile through the split table at $08D6/$09C6.
Stage 3 tile grid from row 2, column 32. The grid has 68 cells per row. Each byte supplies a metatile index to the renderer through the stage row pointers.
Stage 3 tile grid from row 10, column 1. The grid has 68 cells per row. Each byte supplies a metatile index to the renderer through the stage row pointers.
Twenty-two copies of tile $1D follow the declared stage-three tile grid to the start of the two-byte zero fill.
Two zero bytes between the retained edge tiles and the next tile allocation.
Stage 3 grid, 68 entries per row and first 9 rows. The engine uses the low three bits for world-coordinate attribute lookups.
Stage 3 attribute grid from row 10, column 1. The grid has 68 cells per row. Each byte holds the attributes for the matching metatile. The coordinate lookup at $3DFA takes its low three bits.
Twenty-four zero bytes after the last declared stage-three attribute row.
Stage 4 grid, 20 entries per row and first 6 rows. Each byte selects one 4 × 4 character tile through the split table at $08D6/$09C6.
Stage 4 tile grid from row 7, column 1. The grid has 20 cells per row. Each byte supplies a metatile index to the renderer through the stage row pointers.
Four metatile indices, $00, $05, $02 and $05, follow the declared stage-four tile grid and precede the attribute grid at $F3D0.
Stage 4 grid, 20 entries per row and first 6 rows. The engine uses the low three bits for world-coordinate attribute lookups.
Stage 4 attribute grid from row 7, column 1. The grid has 20 cells per row. Each byte holds the attributes for the matching metatile. The coordinate lookup at $3DFA takes its low three bits.
Thirty-six zero bytes after the last declared attribute row and before the scene state at $F480.
Set during alternate-stage initialisation and cleared when the tile update counts no occupied X slots.
Countdown seeded to 80 at $F482 and decremented while the background flash and tile changes run.

Saves the background latch, disables sprites and alternates its bit 3. When the flag at $F480 is set, also increments the extended background colours and advances indexed entries for up to 80 passes before restoring the latch.
Current X columns of the moving blocks. Zero marks a vacant slot. The initializer seeds twenty slots and the shot overlap tests those twenty.
Sixteen zero bytes in the allocation after the scene setup returns.
Current screen rows of moving blocks, including positions above the visible screen.
Hits accumulated per slot. The movement and hit handlers transfer this count when a moving block passes into the next slot.
Sixteen zero bytes inside the loaded state area before the block painter's tables.
Per-slot animation counters. The drawing code shifts this value right twice to select a replacement 42-character pattern.
Sixteen zero bytes before the subsequent pattern allocation.
Saved X columns used by the eraser when the current position or animation changes.
Saved screen rows used by the eraser to find the block's previous position.
Saved animation counts compared with $F513 to trigger redraws.
Row seeds written by $F57C and restored when the lowest block in a column of the formation advances into the next slot.
Row limits indexed by $F891 to decide when a block's state is transferred.
Creates twenty 6-character-wide blocks in four groups of five. Successive X columns and Y rows differ by seven. Clears each block's hit and animation counts and invokes the drawing routine.
Forty-two row-major offsets covering six columns across seven rows on a 40-column screen.
Forty-two character codes for the ordinary moving block.
Forty-two character codes selected by animation counts 12 through 15.
Forty-two character codes selected by animation counts 8 through 11.
Forty-two character codes selected by animation counts 4 through 7.
Four split pointers with high bytes at $F697. The drawing code selects a pattern by shifting the animation count right twice.
Four high address bytes paired with the low bytes at $F693. The renderer patches the indexed character load at $F720.
Return instruction reached by the block renderer when the X column is zero.
Saves this slot's current position and animation as the last drawn state, then copies the selected 42-character pattern to the active drawing page. Skips rows and columns outside its drawable bounds.
Loads one character from the patched block-pattern base indexed by the current cell.
Low byte of the patched block-pattern base.
High byte of the patched block-pattern base. The loop writes the character to the screen and advances the cell indices until all 42 cells have been considered.
The draw helper reloads X with zero before reloading Y and returning.
The draw helper reloads Y with zero before returning.
Repeated 0 through 5 offsets for the seven screen rows, used by the renderer and eraser to clip each column at 40.
Uses the last drawn X column and row saved for the slot. Writes space at each visible cell of the previous 6-by-7 character footprint.
The erase helper reloads X with zero before reloading Y and returning.
The erase helper reloads Y with zero before returning.
Loaded zero between the block eraser's return and the block updater.

Counts occupied slots, tracks their lowest X column, redraws changed positions or animations and decrements the animation counts. With no blocks left clears the active flag. Shifts the player left when the lowest occupied column reaches its position.
Ten-update divider for shifting the next set of moving blocks left.
Chooses one of five start indices for $F850, which shifts entries spaced by five and rotates the start index.
On countdown expiry, decrements the nonzero X columns in the chosen group and rotates the group index.
Tests fifteen slots for space in the next group. Increments the moving block's row, and at its limit transfers X, damage and animation to the next group and resets its old row slot.

On first entry initialises the moving blocks and alternate-stage actors. Later updates the block formation, checks shots and updates the scene. Once the tile-scene flag clears, calls the four follow-on routines.
Accumulates the count of moving-block slots with nonzero X during the scan at $F7E7.
Tests two live shot slots against the 6-by-7 rectangles. Matched shots are stopped and play effects. A block outside its hit cooldown flashes, accumulates a hit and disappears on hit eight.
Eight mask values indexed by the low three bits of the byte at $1904 plus the phase index. The renderer writes the selected masks to $45C0–$45DF.
Low two bits of this incrementing counter gate the column and glyph update at $F9AB.

Updates on every fourth call. Draws seventeen cells in column one using a four-character repeat from $B8, or spaces when $F480 is clear. Sets their colours to seven and updates 32 glyph bytes at $45C0 from the mask table.
Starting index for the source at $1904 during the glyph update. Increments once per draw.
Y position of the first sprite in the three-sprite stack. The other two add $15 and $2A.
Zero holds the base Y steady. One moves up until below $40 and selects two. Two moves down until reaching $78 and selects one.

Updates base Y from the vertical phase, then draws a stack using sprites four through six with pointers $91 through $93 and colour seven. All three share the actor X plus fine scroll and are hidden when its X high byte is two.

Five bytes of state for the moving sprite at $FAB4. The first pair holds integer and fractional Y. The next pair holds signed velocity in high and low bytes. The fifth byte alternates the velocity after impact.
Incremented when the sprite starts moving. The low bit selects the upward velocity when it bounces.

When the sprite is idle and the stack is moving, initializes it near the stack and plays effect seven. Subtracts three from X and increases vertical velocity by one quarter per update. On reaching Y $A6, plays effect four and sets one of two upward velocities. Programs sprite seven from the resulting position.
Loads the enable mask for sprites zero through six and jumps to the VIC enable store at $FBA5.

Requires an active falling sprite and no existing outcome. Checks horizontal distance within six half-resolution units. Uses a vertical threshold selected by player pose before setting outcome one and cooldown $17.

Tests both eligible projectile slots against the stack X and base Y. A hit plays effect two, reduces the remaining count, marks the projectile and starts the stack moving if idle. The last hit sets stage outcome one and clears the contact result.

Retained instruction bytes following the shot-check return. The two chunks at $FC5B and $FC87 match the tail of the Mission 2 sprite-pair and contact routines in shape, with different operands at $FC74 and in the contact test.
Nine loaded zero bytes between the retained scene code and the mission metadata.
The one-based mission number used for this file and for play selection in the resident engine.
Four split pointers with their high bytes at $FCC5. The resident loader at $0B26 selects a stage and gives its grid to the row-pointer builder at $0B46.
High bytes for the tile grids. $0B2B takes the entry for the active stage and puts it in $FC before generating row pointers.
Four split pointers with high bytes at $FCCD. The grid parallels the tile map and the resident coordinate lookup at $3DFA masks each attribute to its low three bits.
High bytes for the attribute grids. $0B35 selects the high byte for $FE.
Stage widths used as a byte stride for the tile and attribute row pointers.
Stage heights used by the resident scaler to derive the vertical playfield limit and by $8EAD to walk the attribute grid.
Indexed stage values copied to $2D during setup by $0AFD.
VIC extended background register $D022 values selected by stage.
VIC extended background register $D023 values selected by stage.
Indexed initial view value written to $1781 before the character drawing loop at $1785.
Four split pointers with high bytes at $FCED. $8FE8 copies 128 bytes from the selected source into a separate workspace half for each player.
High bytes for the placement seeds. $8FF3 selects one for $FC before copying seeds to player workspace.
Indexed stage bytes cached at $0AEA and $0BE0 before display setup.
Stage index compared at $1A82. A match enables the alternate source at $D800 and installs the two operand bytes following this value at $1642/$1643.
Low and high bytes written to $1642/$1643 on the stage selected by $FCF5.
High byte of the alternate stage callback address copied into the resident call at $1641.
Four stage-indexed masks copied to $1901 at $0B11. The resident sprite routines AND their priority bits with this mask before writing VIC register $D01B.
The pair at $FCFC/$FCFD supplies the two operand bytes at $2B0A/$2B0B.
High byte of the pair installed at $2B0A/$2B0B.
Low and high bytes of the mission-provided routine that $1AB3 calls after preparing the stage grids.
High byte of the stage setup call target, installed at $1AB5.
Forty-eight loaded zero bytes between the stage hook directory and the shared bytes at $FD30.

A copy of the sixteen default C64 KERNAL RAM vectors at $0314–$0333. The entries begin with the IRQ, BRK and NMI targets $EA31, $FE66 and $FE47, followed by the BASIC and device I/O hooks. All five mission payloads carry the same copy.
Forty-eight loaded zero bytes between the shared bytes at $FD30 and the stage placement source at $FD80.

Stage 1 placement seed copied into player workspace by $8FE8. A record has a destination low byte, destination high byte and value. A zero value ends the loop that applies records to the working stage grid.
Stage 2 placement seed copied into page $0200. The resident setup applies the value of each record at its two-byte destination and stops at the first zero value.

Placement records shared by stages 3 and 4 in this mission, with an in-game destination word followed by a value byte. The loader supplies $70 bytes of this workspace source before the overlay ends at $FEEF.
